lead.title: Trump administration asks federal court to dismiss its lawsuit over US Senate election in Alaska – live
lead.summary: Democrat Mary Peltola was declared winner earlier this week in highly scrutinized Senate race that featured two Dan Sullivans on the ballot Sign up for the Breaking News US email The National Security Agency is seeing a third day of disruptions to its internal network, NSA Net, which allows staff to share highly classified information with each other , according to the New York Times. The Times reports that employees at the NSA’s Maryland headquarters are under “code orange” for Thursday day shift, which requires non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors. A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed. The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. The vote is scheduled for next month: As things stand, the election is set for 1 December . Both incumbent senators and incoming Democratic members will participate, while retiring and outgoing senators will not vote, despite many having publicly weighed in on the race. Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. Earlier this month, House Republicans selected hardliner Jim Jordan as their leader after Mike Johnson opted not to run for minority leader. In the Senate, Republicans unanimously backed John Thune to continue leading the conference. Continue reading...

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.summary: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. Sports.title: Sandpapergate has gone from a sporting scandal to a rolling loop of outrage and overreaction | Jonathan Horn
Sports.summary: Nothing about the responses and reprisals to Australia’s ball tampering have been proportional in a story where the truth probably lies somewhere in the middle Who said long-form journalism is dead? As Matt Renshaw nudged his ones and twos in an already forgotten ODI match, the broadcasters were scanning Cameron Bancroft’s 4000-word essay . SEN’s Gerard Whateley was calling for a comprehensive judicial inquiry, “a little bit like a coroner’s inquest,” with witnesses compelled to attend and be subjected to cross examination. Cricket Australia’s “forum” , announced a few hours earlier, had already been skittled. Nothing in the eight years since a piece of sandpaper was taken on to the field in Cape Town, including the publication of Usman Khawaja’s book Sabr , had been as revelatory as Bancroft’s first-person account . But as always with this story, we were bracing for the next press conference, the next podcast, the next corroborating statement, the next counterclaim, the next overreaction. Continue reading...
